title: Function Call Blueprint: compact JSON grammar, lenient parser, and humanized errors
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define a compact, backwards-compatible JSON grammar and runtime parsing strategy for function/tool calls that prioritizes developer ergonomics and graceful degradation. This ticket captures the blueprint for a lenient parser, a small set of human-readable error codes, and fallback behaviors to support legacy clients and incremental rollout of stricter validation. Goal: reduce customer friction from schema mismatches while enabling precise diagnostics for prompt engineering and SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Specification doc describing the compact grammar, coercion rules, and backward-compat mapping is reviewed by PM, Design, and Runtime Eng
A2: Runtime implements a lenient parser mode that emits warnings (not hard failures) for common backward-compatible mismatches
A3: A taxonomy of 12 error/warning codes with humanized messages is published and surfaced through API responses and Dashboard
A4: SDKs (Python/JS) include a compatibility shim that maps legacy call shapes to the compact grammar for 95% of observed customer calls
A5: End-to-end tests cover coercion, warning emission, and strict-mode enforcement; CI gate prevents regressions
design_notes: Compact grammar: prefer an object shape with explicit 'name' and 'args' fields; allow args to be object or flat list for legacy callers
Lenient parsing: try best-effort coercions (string->number, single value -> single-element array) and record a structured warning list
Humanized errors: prioritize short codes like E_ARG_MISSING, W_TYPE_COERCED, E_UNEXPECTED_EXTRA for quick triage
Compatibility mapping: provide deterministic mapping rules from legacy shapes (positional arrays, stringified JSON) to canonical args object
Telemetry: include warning counts, example payloads, and a top-k mismatch patterns dashboard for product/SDR feedback
implementation_steps: Step 1: Draft compact grammar RFC and publish to Confluence (owner: Aisha)
Step 2: Implement parser library in runtime repo with two modes: strict, lenient (owner: runtime team)
Step 3: Add warning/error code enum and human-readable mapping in API layer; ensure codes are stable across minor releases
Step 4: Create SDK shims to translate legacy call shapes and emit local warnings where possible (owners: SDK leads)
Step 5: Instrument telemetry and create dashboard in Console showing warning rates and top patterns
Step 6: Run compatibility tests against synthetic corpus of historical customer calls and iterate coercion rules
Step 7: Roll out lenient mode by default with opt-in strict mode; announce deprecation timeline with migration guide
open_decisions: D1: Default mode for hosted API should be 'lenient' to reduce immediate customer breakage or 'strict' to encourage correct schemas? (current proposal: lenient)
D2: Should the runtime auto-coerce date-like strings to ISO date objects, or surface as W_TYPE_COERCED only?
D3: How aggressively should we drop unknown extra fields when mapping legacy shapes—silently drop or surface W_UNEXPECTED_EXTRA?
D4: Storage of example failing payloads: redaction policy and retention window for privacy/compliance
testing_plan: Create unit tests for parser coercions (50+ cases covering numeric/string/boolean/array/object transitions)
Generate large corpus of historical call payloads from telemetry and run compatibility mapper; assert >=95% automated mapping success
Integration tests: SDK->API->runtime round-trip validating warning emission and error codes
Chaos test: inject malformed JSON and ensure runtime returns stable error codes with minimal latency impact
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dogfood deployment in staging and internal apps for 2 weeks
Phase 1: Gradual rollout to 10% of hosted API traffic with feature flag; monitor warning rates and error spikes
Phase 2: 50% rollout with targeted notices to customers emitting frequent warnings, provide migration snippets
Phase 3: Default to lenient for all hosted traffic; enable strict opt-in through API header or account setting
Phase 4: After 6 months, evaluate turning on stricter checks for new customers and provide longer deprecation window for old clients
